title: Component Lab: Surface Scaling Kit + Rollout Token Interop for Cost Views
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a Component Lab and token interoperability layer focused on cost-related surfaces and rollout rails. This ticket scopes a Figma-first exploration and a lightweight reference implementation (component snippets + usage guidance) to ensure consistent behavior across compact/dense/expanded dashboard states and rollout controls. Outcomes: a modular Surface Scaling Kit (spacing, elevation, typography tied to cost density modes), a Rollout Token Interop guide (how rollout states map to visual tokens), and a small set of vetted components for Console teams to adopt (CostCard, RolloutRail, DensityToggle, MiniSparkline).
acceptance_criteria: Figma Component Library published with Surface Scaling Kit symbols and token mapping table
Design spec document that maps rollout states (canary, staged, full) to visual tokens and accessible motion patterns
Three example Console screens (Cost Overview, Route Rollouts, Model Cost Breakdown) implemented as Figma prototypes showing compact/dense/expanded variants
Developer handoff artifacts: CSS/Token export (name-to-value mapping), 1 example React snippet for CostCard with density prop, and QA checklist
Consistency audit run against 8 existing console pages with remediation guidance for mismatches
design_notes: Context: multiple Console teams are independently implementing cost widgets and rollout rails; we see drift in spacing, elevation, and how rollout states surface error/disabled/active styles. Approach: create a small, orthogonal token system that can be applied on top of existing tokens (Density Scale: D0, D1, D2) and a component lab that demonstrates token overrides. Trade-offs: keep token surface minimal to avoid double-layers of tokens while still enabling per-surface adjustments for high-information views (eg. Cost Overview) vs. low-information (eg. Alerts panel). Accessibility: color contrast and focus states must be preserved across density modes and when quantization/compact spacing is applied. Performance: avoid designs that force rasterized assets; prefer vector and CSS where possible. Rollout tokens need to express semantic states rather than raw palette values (e.g., rollout.success-border, rollout.warn-bg).
